data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes policy for the management and use of the Internet in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
This regulation supersedes DR 3300-001-I, Internet, dated March 23, 1999.
The term “agency,” or “agencies and staff offices,” unless otherwise noted in this directive, will be considered to encompass the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices of USDA.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices of USDA
conditions: unless otherwise noted in this directive

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal operating procedures.
conditions: when developing their internal operating procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.

If agencies or staff offices publish a supplement to this DR, one copy of each supplement shall be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG) at ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.
policy_statements.target: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG)
conditions: If agencies or staff offices publish a supplement to this DR

policy_statements.source_text: The Internet is composed of a large number of interconnected worldwide networks ranging from intra-building local area networks (LAN) to global wide-area networks.
Over the years, the Internet has expanded to include Government information, educational information systems, archives, and business resources.
The USDA authorizes the use of the Internet to support Departmental, agency, and staff office missions.

The Internet is an integral part of service delivery at USDA as high-speed networking technologies and developments have made it a desirable source for conducting research, disseminating information, and communicating.
Access to the Internet is provided through the USDA Universal Telecommunications Network (UTN).

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: USDA policy allows and encourages the use of Internet services to support Departmental, agency, and staff office missions.
Users of the Internet shall adhere to the following policy regarding the content and management of Internet data and information.
policy_statements.target: following policy regarding the content and management of Internet data and information

policy_statements.source_text: The Internet may be used for, but is not limited to, the following purposes:
The communication and exchange of data between state and local governments, private sector organizations, and educational and research institutions, both in the United States and abroad;
The development of Internet-based projects;
Interactive sharing of information without compromising USDA secured data;
conditions: without compromising USDA secured data

policy_statements.source_text: The exchange of any non-sensitive data between USDA entities in support of Departmental mission, agency and staff office missions, or other official purposes; and
conditions: between USDA entities
in support of Departmental mission, agency and staff office missions, or other official purposes

policy_statements.source_text: The distribution and collection of information related to official program delivery that is in compliance with Federal and Departmental guidelines.
conditions: that is in compliance with Federal and Departmental guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with the Federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) Council’s Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on “Limited Personal Use” of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology (Limited Personal Use), dated May 19, 1999, employees may use the Internet for personal matters on an occasional basis provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties.
conditions: on an occasional basis
provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties
cross_references: Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on “Limited Personal Use” of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology (Limited Personal Use), dated May 19, 1999

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with the Limited Personal Use guidance, employees must not use the Internet:
To conduct activities that are illegal, inappropriate, or offensive to fellow employees or the public.
Such activities include, but are not limited to, hate speech or material that ridicules others on the basis of race, creed, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin, or sexual orientation;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit sexually explicit or sexually oriented materials;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit materials related to illegal gambling, illegal weapons, terrorist activities, and any other illegal activities or activities otherwise prohibited;
To conduct activities that could cause congestion, delay, or disruption of service to any Government system or equipment.
For example, video or other large file attachments can degrade the performance of the entire network;
For commercial purposes or in support of for-profit activities or other outside employment or business activity (e.g., consulting for pay or sales of goods and services);
To engage in any outside fundraising activity, endorse any product or service, participate in any lobbying activity, or engage in any prohibited partisan political activity;
To post Departmental information to external newsgroups, bulletin boards, or other public forums without authority; and
conditions: without authority

policy_statements.source_text: To conduct activities that could generate more than a minimal expense to the Government.

In accordance with the Limited Personal Use, it is the responsibility of employees to ensure they are not giving the false impression that they are acting in an official capacity when they are using Government equipment for non-Government purposes.
conditions: when they are using Government equipment for non-Government purposes
policy_statements.target: false impression that they are acting in an official capacity

policy_statements.source_text: If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent an agency or staff office, then an adequate disclaimer must be used.
conditions: If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent an agency or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: One acceptable disclaimer is “The contents of this message are mine personally and do not reflect any position of the Government or my agency.”
USDA employees have no reasonable expectation of privacy regarding any communications involving, or data transiting or stored on, any Government telecommunications system.
At any time, the Government may for any lawful government purpose monitor, intercept, search, and seize any communication, or data transiting or stored, on a Government telecommunications system.
policy_statements.target: any communication, or data transiting or stored, on a Government telecommunications system
conditions: for any lawful government purpose

policy_statements.source_text: Any communications involving, or data transiting or stored, on any Government telecommunications system may be disclosed or used for any lawful government purpose.
conditions: for any lawful government purpose

policy_statements.source_text: Use of Government telecommunications systems, including incidental and personal use, whether authorized or unauthorized, implies the employee’s consent to monitoring, which is final and irrevocable.

Employees may not rely on any statements or informal policies purporting to provide any expectation of privacy on Government telecommunications systems, whether oral or written, by any other official, except USDA’s Chief Information Officer.
policy_statements.target: any statements or informal policies purporting to provide any expectation of privacy on Government telecommunications systems

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA UTN shall be used exclusively by USDA agencies and staff offices to connect to the Internet except in instances where a waiver to the use of the UTN has been granted by the ENS Director.
conditions: except in instances where a waiver to the use of the UTN has been granted by the ENS Director

policy_statements.source_text: Information about waivers is provided in Section 7 of this DR.

The USDA UTN shall use the most current General Services Administration (GSA) approved contract for circuits to connect to the Internet and to transport inter-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA) data between USDA agencies and staff offices via the Internet.
policy_statements.target: most current General Services Administration (GSA) approved contract

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum for Chief Information Officers of Executive Department and Agencies, Transition to IPv6, dated September 28, 2010, specifies that the Federal Government must transition to IPv6 in order to:
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum for Chief Information Officers of Executive Department and Agencies, Transition to IPv6, dated September 28, 2010

policy_statements.source_text: Enable the successful deployment and expansion of key Federal information technology (IT) modernization initiatives, such as Cloud Computing, Broadband, and SmartGrid, which rely on robust, scalable Internet networks;
Reduce complexity and increase transparency of Internet services by eliminating the architectural need to rely on Network Address Translation (NAT) technologies;
Enable ubiquitous security services for end-to-end network communications that will serve as the foundation for securing future Federal IT systems; and
Enable the Internet to continue to operate efficiently through an integrated, well-engineered networking platform and accommodate the future expansion of Internet-based services.

The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), 48 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 11.002 (g), sets the requirements for OMB’s goal that Federal agencies include IPv6 compliance when buying networked IT products.
cross_references: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), 48 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 11.002 (g)

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with the OMB memorandum and FAR, all contracts that include the acquisition of IT using Internet Protocol (IP) must contain IPv6 contract clause language.
conditions: that include the acquisition of IT using Internet Protocol (IP)

policy_statements.source_text: This language can be found in USDA Procurement Advisory 127, Acquiring Information Technology - Recommended Language to Comply with Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6).
cross_references: USDA Procurement Advisory 127, Acquiring Information Technology - Recommended Language to Comply with Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6)

policy_statements.source_text: To access the Internet via the USDA UTN, agencies and staff offices must use officially registered USDA IP addresses as explained in DR 3300-001-M, Internet Protocol (IP) Addresses.
conditions: To access the Internet via the USDA UTN

policy_statements.source_text: Official IP addresses uniquely distinguish each host or device connected to the network.
The OCIO, ENS is the IP addressing and domain name registration authority for USDA.
policy_statements.resulting_status: IP addressing and domain name registration authority

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices shall not connect a host or other device that uses IP and has an unregistered IP address to the Internet, the USDA UTN, or to any network connected to either of these networks.
policy_statements.target: host or other device that uses IP and has an unregistered IP address
conditions: that uses IP and has an unregistered IP address

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices will modify their IP addressing plans to include the planned efficiencies and to bring all existing IP addresses in compliance with DR 3300-001-M.
USDA connections to the internet allow many types of threat activities to be executed against the USDA IT infrastructure.

Threat activities range from social threats such as phishing, spam, password guessing, visiting malware infected websites, exploitation of application vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, and data-malformation.
To defend USDA IT assets against the diverse types of weaknesses and threats, a series of cybersecurity policies are continually being created and updated.
USDA cybersecurity policies can be found in the USDA 3500 to 3599 Series cybersecurity directives.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Inspector General Act of 1978, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Appendix 3, Sections 1-12, the Office of the Inspector General is exempt from the provisions in this directive for mission-related activities only.
conditions: for mission-related activities only
cross_references: Inspector General Act of 1978, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Appendix 3, Sections 1-12

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
In accordance with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA) of December 19, 2014:
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA) of December 19, 2014

policy_statements.source_text: Establish processes to regularly engage with program managers to evaluate IT resources supporting the strategic objectives of agency and staff offices;
policy_statements.target: IT resources supporting the strategic objectives of agency and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Define enterprise policy for the level of detail of planned expenditure reporting for all transactions that include IT resources;
policy_statements.target: enterprise policy for the level of detail of planned expenditure reporting for all transactions that include IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: Define the development processes, milestones, review gates, and the overall polices for all capital planning, enterprise architecture (EA), project management, and reporting for IT resources;
policy_statements.target: development processes, milestones, review gates, and the overall polices for all capital planning, enterprise architecture (EA), project management, and reporting for IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: Approve any movement of funds for IT resources that require Congressional notification; and
policy_statements.target: any movement of funds for IT resources that require Congressional notification

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct TechStat reviews, or use other applicable performance measurements to evaluate the use of IT resources.
Represent the USDA to the Federal CIO Council, GSA, and OMB regarding requests for exceptions to mandatory telecommunications services contracts;
policy_statements.target: Federal CIO Council, GSA, and OMB

policy_statements.target: oversight agencies, such as OMB, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Commerce (DOC), and Federal Communications Commission (FCC)

Serve as the USDA liaison with international, interLATA and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (intraLATA) telecommunications service providers; and

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA representative to the Diplomatic Telecommunications Service Program Office (DTSPO).
The ENS Director will:
Establish procedures for monitoring, measuring, and enforcing compliance with this DR;

policy_statements.target: agency and staff office compliance with USDA Internet policies and procedures

Maintain a database of approved private ISPs used by agencies and staff offices in lieu of the USDA Access Network;

Ensure agency and staff office personnel comply with this directive;

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes policy for the management and use of the Internet in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
This regulation supersedes DR 3300-001-I, *Internet*, dated March 23, 1999
The term “agency,” or “agencies and staff offices,” unless otherwise noted in this directive, will be considered to encompass the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices of USDA.

The Internet is composed of a large number of interconnected worldwide networks ranging from intra-building local area networks (LAN) to global wide-area networks.
Over the years, the Internet has expanded to include Government information, educational information systems, archives, and business resources.
The USDA authorizes the use of the Internet to support Departmental, agency, and staff office missions.

The Internet is an integral part of service delivery at USDA as high-speed networking technologies and developments have made it a desirable source for conducting research, disseminating information, and communicating.
Access to the Internet is provided through the USDA Universal Telecommunications Network (UTN).

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.
all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA
USDA policy allows and encourages the use of Internet services to support Departmental, agency, and staff office missions.
Users of the Internet shall adhere to the following policy regarding the content and management of Internet data and information.
following policy regarding the content and management of Internet data and information
The Internet may be used for, but is not limited to, the following purposes:
The communication and exchange of data between state and local governments, private sector organizations, and educational and research institutions, both in the United States and abroad;
Interactive sharing of information without compromising USDA secured data;
The exchange of any non-sensitive data between USDA entities in support of Departmental mission, agency and staff office missions, or other official purposes; and
in support of Departmental mission, agency and staff office missions, or other official purposes
The distribution and collection of information related to official program delivery that is in compliance with Federal and Departmental guidelines.
that is in compliance with Federal and Departmental guidelines

(2) In accordance with the Federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) Council’s  *Recommended Executive Branch Model Policy/Guidance on “Limited Personal Use” of Government Office Equipment Including Information Technology*  (*Limited Personal Use*), dated May 19, 1999, employees may use the Internet for personal matters on an occasional basis provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties.
provided that there is no loss of employee productivity or interference with official employee duties
In accordance with the *Limited Personal Use* guidance, employees must not use the Internet
To conduct activities that are illegal, inappropriate, or offensive to fellow employees or the public.
Such activities include, but are not limited to, hate speech or material that ridicules others on the basis of race, creed, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin, or sexual orientation;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit sexually explicit or sexually oriented materials;
To create, download, view, store, copy, or transmit materials related to illegal gambling, illegal weapons, terrorist activities, and any other illegal activities or activities otherwise prohibited;
To conduct activities that could cause congestion, delay, or disruption of service to any Government system or equipment.
For example, video or other large file attachments can degrade the performance of the entire network;
For commercial purposes or in support of for-profit activities or other outside employment or business activity (e.g., consulting for pay or sales of goods and services);
To engage in any outside fundraising activity, endorse any product or service, participate in any lobbying activity, or engage in any prohibited partisan political activity;
To post Departmental information to external newsgroups, bulletin boards, or other public forums without authority; and
To conduct activities that could generate more than a minimal expense to the Government.

In accordance with the *Limited Personal Use*, it is the responsibility of employees to ensure they are not giving the false impression that they are acting in an official capacity when they are using Government equipment for non-Government purposes
when they are using Government equipment for non-Government purposes
false impression that they are acting in an official capacity
If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent an agency or staff office, then an adequate disclaimer must be used.
If there is an expectation that such a personal use could be interpreted to represent an agency or staff office
One acceptable disclaimer is “The contents of this message are mine personally and do not reflect any position of the Government or my agency.”
USDA employees have no reasonable expectation of privacy regarding any communications involving, or data transiting or stored on, any Government telecommunications system.
At any time, the Government may for any lawful government purpose monitor, intercept, search, and seize any communication, or data transiting or stored, on a Government telecommunications system.
any communication, or data transiting or stored, on a Government telecommunications system
Any communications involving, or data transiting or stored, on any Government telecommunications system may be disclosed or used for any lawful government purpose.
Use of Government telecommunications systems, including incidental and personal use, whether authorized or unauthorized, implies the employee’s consent to monitoring, which is final and irrevocable.

Employees may not rely on any statements or informal policies purporting to provide any expectation of privacy on Government telecommunications systems, whether oral or written, by any other official, except USDA’s Chief Information Officer.
any statements or informal policies purporting to provide any expectation of privacy on Government telecommunications systems
The USDA UTN shall be used exclusively by USDA agencies and staff offices to connect to the Internet except in instances where a waiver to the use of the UTN has been granted by the ENS Director.
except in instances where a waiver to the use of the UTN has been granted by the ENS Director
Information about waivers is provided in Section 7 of this DR.

The USDA UTN shall use the most current General Services Administration (GSA) approved contract for circuits to connect to the Internet and to transport inter-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA) data between USDA agencies and staff offices via the Internet.
most current General Services Administration (GSA) approved contract

(1) The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum for Chief Information Officers of Executive Department and Agencies,  *Transition to IPv6* , dated September 28, 2010, specifies that the Federal Government must transition to IPv6 in order to:

Enable the successful deployment and expansion of key Federal information technology (IT) modernization initiatives, such as Cloud Computing, Broadband, and SmartGrid, which rely on robust, scalable Internet networks;
Reduce complexity and increase transparency of Internet services by eliminating the architectural need to rely on Network Address Translation (NAT) technologies;
Enable ubiquitous security services for end-to-end network communications that will serve as the foundation for securing future Federal IT systems; and
Enable the Internet to continue to operate efficiently through an integrated, well-engineered networking platform and accommodate the future expansion of Internet-based services.
In accordance with the OMB memorandum and FAR, all contracts that include the acquisition of IT using Internet Protocol (IP) must contain IPv6 contract clause language.
that include the acquisition of IT using Internet Protocol (IP)
(1) To access the Internet via the USDA UTN, agencies and staff offices must use officially registered USDA IP addresses as explained in  DR 3300-001-M , *Internet Protocol (IP) Addresses*.
To access the Internet via the USDA UTN
Official IP addresses uniquely distinguish each host or device connected to the network.
The OCIO, ENS is the IP addressing and domain name registration authority for USDA.
IP addressing and domain name registration authority

Agencies and staff offices shall not connect a host or other device that uses IP and has an unregistered IP address to the Internet, the USDA UTN, or to any network connected to either of these networks.

that uses IP and has an unregistered IP address
Agencies and staff offices will modify their IP addressing plans to include the planned efficiencies and to bring all existing IP addresses in compliance with DR 3300-001-M.
USDA connections to the internet allow many types of threat activities to be executed against the USDA IT infrastructure.

Threat activities range from social threats such as phishing, spam, password guessing, visiting malware infected websites, exploitation of application vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, and data-malformation.
To defend USDA IT assets against the diverse types of weaknesses and threats, a series of cybersecurity policies are continually being created and updated.
USDA cybersecurity policies can be found in the USDA  3500 to 3599 Series  cybersecurity directives.

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes policy for the management and use of the Internet in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.
